name: History of the Earth
description: The 4.5 billion years of the planet: its birth, the first life, the ages of the Earth and the five mass extinctions.

checkpoints.name: The early Earth
checkpoints.note: The Earth forms from dust and rock, is struck by a Mars-sized body that throws out the Moon, and is pounded by impacts while its surface cools enough for the first oceans.

checkpoints.name: First life
checkpoints.note: Single cells rule the planet for billions of years. Microbes fill the air with oxygen, ice may cover the globe, and the first soft-bodied animals appear at the very end.

checkpoints.name: Life fills the seas and the land
checkpoints.note: Animals explode into variety, plants and then four-limbed descendants of fish move onto land, coal forests grow, and the continents merge into Pangaea before the worst extinction in history empties the world.

checkpoints.name: The age of dinosaurs
checkpoints.note: Life recovers and dinosaurs take over. Pangaea splits and new oceans open, until an asteroid strikes Mexico and ends the age of the great reptiles.

checkpoints.name: The age of mammals
checkpoints.note: Mountains such as the Himalayas rise as drifting plates collide, an idea now called plate tectonics. The climate cools into ice ages, mammals spread, and Homo sapiens arrives late. Humans now change the planet, which some call a new age, the Anthropocene.
